missing_units.reason: No unit judged GHSA-hw8m-q44c-ggrf. The only rating is context/research/2026-10-18-wasmtime-49-advisories.md:73 ('no - GC proposal'), the same premise h17 showed false for GHSA-m63x: the binaries carry +exception-handling, 44,791 try_table, 26,569 throw_ref and an exnref in their type section (h17's wjc8 check), and wasmtime keeps exception objects in its GC heap, so exnref is a GC reference. _engines.py#_engine (lines 110-127) sets only consume_fuel, epoch_interruption and the stack sizes, so GC and exceptions are on in both engines; uv.lock resolves wasmtime 49.0.0, inside the advisory's range (fixed 49.0.2). The advisory affects 'every Wasmtime version with GC and exceptions' and its only workaround is disabling exceptions, which _engine does not. h17's unit was scoped to m63x, p79w and wjc8; h12 counted only br_table; docs/explanation/security-model.md:60 tells users only two later-fixed advisories reach a guest. The same reachability question (does ordinary guest Python drive a C++ throw/catch or a longjmp through these try_table pads, e.g. a pybind11 exception conversion in matplotlib or HiGHS in scipy.optimize) is exactly what Phase 3 left open for wasmtime-49.0.0:GHSA-m63x-6p34-q65x:try_table-catch-fuel, so one unit can settle both: count catch_ref/catch_all_ref pads with a call between the landing and throw_ref, name guest-Python entry points that reach them, and compare python.wasm under wasmtime CLI 49.0.3 (fixed) with wasmtime-py 49.0.0 on that path.
